quotes.text: Autopilot doesn't wipe a device and push a custom copy of windows onto it. Instead, it uses the version of windows that already shipped on the machine and configures it from the cloud.

takeaways: Windows Autopilot configures the Windows that already ships on a device from the cloud instead of re-imaging it.
A device is claimed through its hardware hash, gets instructions from a deployment profile, joins Microsoft Entra ID and is then managed by Intune.
Deployment modes and the newer Device Preparation flavor trade flexibility against speed, while internet access, TPM chips and licensing remain real prerequisites.
hook: Handing out a new work laptop used to mean imaging, driver packs and a trip to the IT desk. This beginner-friendly episode explains Windows Autopilot for IT newcomers and business users: hardware hashes, deployment profiles, Entra join, Intune and the deployment modes. You will understand how a device can belong to your organization before anyone opens the box.
